clue.text: Stopped after bad upset

indicators.note: after says the first word named is placed second, behind the one for bad

blocks.note: food that has gone bad has gone off
something stopped has ended

explanation.surface: Someone halted after a nasty upset, as in a race or match gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the word for stopped after the word for bad, so the clue reads back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be offended is to be hurt and annoyed by a slight, a past-tense synonym for upset.

clue.text: Located article, one among many with sound structural basis

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the single digit goes inside the word for many

blocks.note: to locate is to find
the indefinite article
Roman numeral one
tons, informally, means a great many
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: A building survey: a sound-structured base found, one of several.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman one goes after the first letter of the word for many; 'sound' then reads as a noun, not as solid.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation stone is the first block laid at a building's base, and figuratively anything that underpins something.

clue.text: Precise demand

blocks.note: first meaning: accurate in every detail
second meaning: to insist on and obtain, as a price

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a demand that is precise; the two words are separate meanings, an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for being correct in detail and a verb for extracting payment or obedience.

clue.text: Challenge lawyer on limits of role

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, so only its first and last letters count

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
the end letters of this word

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a lawyer about the boundaries of their job.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the lawyer sits over the end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dare is a challenge to do something risky, and as a verb to dare someone is to challenge them.

clue.text: Throw party before noon? Sure thing

blocks.note: a disco is a dance party
N is an abbreviation for noon
a cert, short for certainty, is a racing term for a sure winner

explanation.surface: Throwing a party before midday? Definitely, says someone keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' poses as the verb of throwing a party, but it is the definition, in the sense of unsettle.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to confuse or fluster them, which is exactly what disconcert means.

clue.text: Time beside stream making tremulous sound

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a rill is a small brook or rivulet

explanation.surface: Sitting by a brook for a while, one hears a quavering noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A trill is a rapid quavering alternation of notes, as in birdsong, which makes it a wavering vibrating noise.

clue.text: Number filled with energy supporting team initially roared

indicators.note: something filled with an item holds it inside, so the energy letter goes into the number
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
a hundred is a number
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fans in their hundreds, full of energy behind their team, roared.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' means sitting below, so the filled number goes under the team's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundered means made a loud deep booming noise, as a crowd or voice does when it roars.

clue.text: Online scan quite absurdly trivial

indicators.note: something absurd is nonsensical, so these letters are rearranged into a ridiculous jumble

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that some internet search was pointless and petty.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsequential means of no importance or consequence, the same as trifling or trivial.

clue.text: Speaker's moral decline

indicators.note: a speaker's word is one heard spoken, so we want a word that sounds the same

blocks.note: the moral of a story is its lesson

explanation.surface: An orator laments a decline in moral standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' reads as a noun in the surface but is a verb here, to grow smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen is to diminish or reduce, as to decline is to fall away in amount.

clue.text: Personnel murmur nervously near informants

indicators.note: acting nervously means fidgeting and jumbled, so the next word's letters are jittered out of order

blocks.note: to hum is to make a low murmur
the four letters of this word, rearranged
a journalist's informants are their sources

explanation.surface: Office staff muttering anxiously close to the company snitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Human resources is the department, and by extension the staff, that a company employs; personnel is the older name for it.

clue.text: Trade show's objective

blocks.note: first meaning: an exhibition of goods for buyers
second meaning: impartial, unbiased

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'objective' as a noun, the aim of a trade show; it is the adjective for even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is an exhibition or market, and fair as an adjective means just and without bias.

clue.text: Check praise, omitting line with appeal

indicators.note: omitting means leaving something out, so one letter is dropped from the word for praise

blocks.note: to laud is to praise
L is the abbreviation for line
IT is an old slang word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Instructions to vet a commendation, dropping a line that is too appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts, so to audit is to examine or verify them.

clue.text: Tapering object outside study, small telescope

indicators.note: the first object sits outside, wrapping round the words that follow it

blocks.note: a cone narrows to a point
a den is a private room for work or study
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A list of things on an astronomer's desk: a pointed object, a study, a little telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telescope' looks like the noun of the surface, but here it is the verb: to shorten by sliding sections together.
explanation.definitionFit: To telescope a story or schedule is to compress it into less space or time, which is what condensing does.

clue.text: Translation of Virgil, deep and rich

indicators.note: a translation renders words in a new form, so the letters are recast in another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A classicist praises a Latin rendering of the poet as profound and lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: Privileged people enjoy wealth and advantages, so the word serves as a looser synonym for well-off.

clue.text: Values cherished by democrat especially

indicators.note: something cherished is held close, so the letters are held inside the following words

blocks.note: the tail of the first word joined to the head of the second

explanation.surface: Principles that a member of the Democratic party holds especially dear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Values' a noun for principles; it is the verb, to assess worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to estimate its worth, so rates and values are both verbs of judgement.

clue.text: Meet and mix endlessly over year, apparently

indicators.note: without an end, so the word for mix loses its final letter

blocks.note: to see someone is to meet them
to mingle is to mix
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Friends who apparently meet up and socialise without pause all year long.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the year letter comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemingly means as far as appearances go, the same as apparently or ostensibly.

clue.text: Instrument in place for playing arrangement

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a British public park for games
an order is an arrangement or sequence

explanation.surface: A musical instrument being set out for a playing arrangement in a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'playing' sound like performing; here it is children's play, in a REC, the British short name for a recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The recorder is a woodwind instrument, the end-blown flute familiar from school music lessons.

clue.text: Doctor, traveller around east also

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the traveller wraps itself about the compass point

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a rover is a wanderer
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A physician and a wanderer who also roam the eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass letter goes in after the first letter of the traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover is an adverb adding a further point, exactly as also or besides does at the start of a sentence.

clue.text: Complete expression of distaste for money

blocks.note: to do a job is to complete it
the interjection of disgust

explanation.surface: A wholehearted grimace of disgust at money, from someone above such things.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is long-standing slang for cash, as bread also is.

clue.text: Command given to dog in list

blocks.note: first meaning: the order to walk close behind
second meaning: of a ship, to lean over to one side

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a list of dog commands; 'list' is the nautical verb for tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer tells a dog to stay close behind, and a ship that keels over to one side is said to do the same word.

clue.text: Top mimic capturing monster, right away

indicators.note: with the right taken away, the R abbreviation is removed from the monster
capturing means seizing and holding, so the mimic wraps round the monster

blocks.note: to ape is to imitate
an ogre is a monster of folklore

explanation.surface: An impressionist imitating a monster nabs it straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right comes out of the monster before it goes inside the mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is a highest point or climax, originally the furthest point of an orbit from the Earth.

clue.text: Sweet not well covered with marzipan?

indicators.note: covered with means coated all round, so the second word wraps the first like icing

blocks.note: marzipan is almond paste
someone not well is ill

explanation.surface: A cake-decorating riddle: a confection that is coated in marzipan and feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that marzipan is defined by example: it is one kind of paste.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small chewable sweet or lozenge, often fruit-flavoured or medicated.

clue.text: Formerly storing uranium, tiny amount

indicators.note: a thing storing something keeps it inside, so the element symbol is placed within

blocks.note: once means at some former time
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A place that once kept uranium now holds only a trace of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, used figuratively for the slightest bit, as in not an ounce of sense.

clue.text: More trouble with book out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the abbreviation for book is taken away

blocks.note: bother is trouble or fuss
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Further hassle with a book that has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean additional or further, as in a few other ideas, so it stands in for more.

clue.text: Language used by chauffeur dutifully

indicators.note: the letters wanted are employed within the next words themselves, sitting in plain view

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: The tongue spoken by a dutiful private driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Composer from south in going here grew excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and agitated, so they are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer from the American South whose excitement grew as he arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The south letter sits in among the three words before the whole lot is reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin wrote Rhapsody in Blue and Porgy and Bess, making him one of America's best-known twentieth-century musicians.

clue.text: People in revolution breaking heart of fogeyish opponent

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for people is read the other way
the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are taken
breaking into something splits it apart, so the people sit inside the middle letters

blocks.note: the two central letters of an eight-letter word
men means people in general

explanation.surface: Rebels storming the heart of a stuffy old-fashioned adversary.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is someone hostile to you, an adversary or foe in war or rivalry.

clue.text: Spirit in amusing prelude to announcement of winner

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the word for amusing

blocks.note: droll means wryly funny
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A drinker gets amusingly tipsy just before the winner is named.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumroll is the sustained rapid drumbeat used to build suspense before a big reveal such as naming a prize-winner.
